title: Four actual order-three elements, the canonical closed image and the original cusp comparison
proved_results: The actual quotient M_all/F is C2 times S3 with its named coset maps; the full positive centralizers of the original s and j are both <t>.

The full normalizer of the original order-three factor in M_all is an actual S3. Its negative involution is constructed from the full factor-conjugacy transporter and transported through the accepted original J-class map to j.

The set K of all nonidentity order-three elements of the actual M inverted by j has exactly four elements. Both the subgroup orbit map from <t> and its inverse, and the four-element generator parametrization and inverse, are explicit.

Each kappa defines the actual Phi_kappa:M->M with tau->t and xi->kappa. All four maps have the same canonical closed image H3, and H3 intersect F equals the image of each original free-group restriction.

The full source P0 is identified with V4 amalg_C2 S3 by explicit inverse generator maps. Its actual map to M_all has the specified finite vertex embeddings, exact edge intersection and quotient isomorphism. Its full image remains unproved.
Every Phi_kappa obeys both exact original involution intertwinings. Its F-abelian matrix is nu_kappa times I or theta according to the named S3 coset sign.

The coefficients are nu0,nu0,-nu0,-nu0, with the canonical positive-conjugacy orientation nu0. Actual section classes force its 2-adic unit coordinate; the full M-abelian map forces nu0=1 modulo three. The coset sign epsilon and conjugacy sign sigma are retained separately.
The full-unit zero space of kappa^(-1)t kappa^(-1)=w^(-1)p^nu w is homeomorphic to the original T. Both transports retain the original h and all original cusp markings.

The continuous parameter is forced to be nu_kappa, yielding the exact four-element cusp-word set formula for T. The full original abelian cusp defect is explicitly calculated and forces nu_kappa=epsilon_kappa*m at a zero.
The original standard h=1 recovers all four full automorphisms and exactly the two already accepted original +/-1 cusp solutions, with full-word failures for the remaining two choices.
